title: Trelcatius: intellect’s object divine truth — will’s object singular grace in Christ
source_text: XXVI. Non absimili modo Trelcatius, dum viveret, in Academia Leydensi Professor, distinguit objectum fidei ratione intellectus, & ratione voluntatis. Objectum, inquit, respectu intellectus, est veritas divina; respectu voluntatis, est singularis Dei gratia, promissionibus exposita in Christo Jesu. Utrumque autem verbo Dei continetur & circumscribitur; quod totum & solum, tanquam objectum suum adaequatum amplectitur fides; & in eo Christum crucifixum cum omnibus suis beneficiis, tanquam objectum suum principale, primum, proximum, & proprium. In Institutione Locorum communium, titulo de fide.
pass_a_gloss: In a not unlike way Trelcatius, while he lived Professor in the Academy of Leiden, distinguishes the object of faith by reason of the intellect, and by reason of the will. The object, he says, with respect to the intellect is divine truth; with respect to the will, is the singular grace of God set forth in the promises in Christ Jesus. But both are contained and circumscribed by the word of God; which whole and alone faith embraces as its adequate object; and in it Christ crucified with all His benefits, as its principal, first, proximate, and proper object. In the Institution of Common Places, under the title on faith.
pass_b_english: Trelcatius (Leiden): object of faith by intellect vs by will.
Intellect: divine truth. Will: singular grace promised in Christ Jesus.
Both bounded by God’s word — faith’s adequate object.
In that Word: crucified Christ with all benefits — principal, first, proximate, proper object.
